dedupe_keys.name: water supply forecast rodeo seasonal streamflow volume forecasting dataset and winning models for 26 western us sites bureau of reclamation and drivendata

description: The Water Supply Forecast Rodeo was a data science competition, sponsored by the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation and hosted by DrivenData, to improve seasonal water supply forecasts that Western US water managers use to run reservoirs, flood control, hydropower and environmental releases. Its assembled datasets and the prize-winning models are published for reuse. Coverage: probabilistic forecasts of naturalised cumulative streamflow volume over seasonal periods at 26 sites in the Western United States, with a hindcast stage validated on 10 years of history, near-real-time forecasts during the 2024 season and a final cross-validation over historical streamflow; participants drew on more than two dozen sources such as antecedent streamflow, snowpack, meteorology, seasonal forecasts and climate teleconnection indices. Format and access: forecast-stage and final-stage data on DrivenData competition pages (which need a free DrivenData login), code for external data sources and all winning solutions with model reports on GitHub; 64 teams submitted, with $500,000 in prizes, completed July 2024. Licence: the data are free to use outside the challenge with attribution; the winning code is MIT. Caveats: the data files were not opened because the data pages require a login, non-winning cross-validation scores are self-reported, and the forecasts cover only 26 sites. Simulation uses: benchmarking seasonal inflow forecasts that drive reservoir operation, drought capacity planning and climate adaptation of Western water supply and hydropower. Related records: the USGS water data APIs (data-usgs-water-data-apis) supply observed streamflow of the kind used as model inputs.
